item.title: ‘Everything Has Been So Cleaned Up’: Modern Imitations Lack Nan Goldin’s Immediacy
item.description: The photographer’s The Ballad of Sexual Dependency captured 1970s and 1980s New York counterculture with an unabashed honesty that photographers and brands today are still desperately hoping to emulate.

item.title: Switzerland’s Rietberg Museum to Return Benin Bronzes
item.description: Works originally looted by the British in 1897 will be returned to Nigeria in a move the mayor of Zurich says is a way of “actively rectifying past injustices”.

item.title: Pizza the Action: Hong Kong Artists Critique ‘Hegemonic’ Venice Model
item.description: Local artists rail against Venice’s “cultural homogenisation” by creating a parallel space where art‑making “doesn’t always have to be serious or career‑driven”.

item.title: Make It Big: New Museum Reopens with an Epic Overview of Humanity
item.description: What is the most revolutionary moment of progress in human history? Four artists whose work is part of the monumental reopening of the New Museum in New York City share the ideas that influence their creative practice.

item.title: Lily Allen ‘West End Girl’ Portrait Unveiled at London’s National Portrait Gallery
item.description: The exhibition of the portrait marks another step in a trend towards uniting pop culture with fine art institutions.

item.title: The Shows and Sights Not to Miss During Hong Kong Art Week
item.description: From literary talks to Michelin‑recommended restaurants, and pop‑ups to buzzing bars, here’s Ocula ’s locally sourced round‑up of where to go during Hong Kong Art Week.

item.title: Agosto Machado, Chinese-Spanish-Filipino-American Artist, Has Died
item.description: The performance artist and gay rights activist who never revealed his true age, saying ‘a lady never tells’, became an archivist of the ephemera left behind by friends lost to AIDS.

item.title: Pure Intention: Is Singapore Biennale About Creativity or Regulation?
item.description: The eighth edition of the Singapore Biennale promotes two distinct ideas: placing art into the everyday and exploring the role of the state in creating cultural infrastructure. Which matters most?

item.title: Ai Weiwei Will Re-enact Prison Detention in 24-Hour Performance
item.description: Audiences in Manchester will be able to watch a 24‑hour reconstruction of the artist and activist’s 2011 incarceration as part of a larger exhibition considering Chinese‑British relations.

item.title: Banned South African Pavilion Artist Defies Government With Venice Show
item.description: Gabrielle Goliath, whose Venice performance commemorating Palestinian civilians was blocked by the South African government, will now show the work during the biennale.
